spec.description: Cosecant branches with supplied axis labels and dashed asymptotes; no grid.
spec.mathematics: y=1/sin(x), 0<x<2pi, x not equal pi; turning points (pi/2,1), (3pi/2,-1).
spec.answerVisibility: Curve and visible axis ticks retained as givens pending resolution of source answer visibility.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{cosec}\frac{\pi}{2}&=\frac{1}{1}=1\\\operatorname{cosec}\frac{3\pi}{2}&=\frac{1}{-1}=-1.\end{align*}$$
Label the turning points $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},1\right)$ and $\left(\frac{3\pi}{2},-1\right)$. Since $\sin x=0$ at $x=0,\pi,2\pi$, these are vertical asymptotes.

spec.description: Complete cosecant graph labelled with both turning points.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\sec0&=\frac{1}{1}=1\\\sec\pi&=\frac{1}{-1}=-1\\\sec2\pi&=\frac{1}{1}=1.\end{align*}$$
Label $(0,1)$, $(\pi,-1)$ and $(2\pi,1)$. Since $\cos x=0$ at $x=\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{3\pi}{2}$, these are vertical asymptotes.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\cot\frac{\pi}{2}&=\frac{0}{1}=0\\\cot\frac{3\pi}{2}&=\frac{0}{-1}=0.\end{align*}$$
Label the intercepts $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},0\right)$ and $\left(\frac{3\pi}{2},0\right)$. Since $\sin x=0$ at $x=0,\pi,2\pi$, these are vertical asymptotes.
